body: I couldn't reproduce the error line disappearing behind the warning, it does seem like a rendering issue. With it blinking with the caret, it reminded me of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116017

Looks good!

Partially addresses https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1005
The rest of it (the tooltips) and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13105 can be done in another PR.

The proposal comments mention the error line highlighting being toned down or removed, but that will have to wait until after underlines also work for the shader editor and json files.

The GDScript and core changes look good to me. There is a slight off-by-one issue though. For errors the ranges seem to be one char longer than they should be (not noticeable in your screenshot since the error ends at the last char on the line): As compared to VSCode You are probably missing an adjustment somewhere because the `ScriptLanguage` column numbers are one-based.

Works well in my testing.

Haven't looked at the editor and gui code. The GDScript stuff LGTM the core stuff too. 

I don't think a dedicated core review is necessary, since all changes are related to the editor specific parts of `ScriptLanguage` but if someone from core wants to double check, be my guest.

Tested locally, it works as expected. Code and design look good to me. ### 100% editor scale Default | Light -|- | ### 150% editor scale Default | Light -|- | ### 200% editor scale Default | Light -|- | **Edit:** Seeing the above screenshots scaled down to 100% makes me realize that line spacing currently depends on editor scale somewhat. This should be fixed in a separate PR. Underlines appear thicker at higher editor scales (relative to the current editor scale), but I know why this is happening. Fixing this can be done in a separate PR as there are many other locations in other Control nodes where it occurs, but it's fairly involved: - The editor uses the `disabled` stretch mode, and increases the font size according to the editor scale. At higher font sizes, the underline thickness automatically increases. - Intuitively, I'd say projects with the `canvas_items` stretch mode don't automatically increase their font size. Instead, oversampling does the job. Therefore, underline thickness doesn't automatically increase. In fact, `theme_cache.base_scale` is not automatically increased either; it's a project setting that can be set only at startup, not at runtime. Therefore, no scaling actually occurs if you use the `canvas_items` stretch mode and just rely on Godot's automatic scaling. - However, testing with LinkButton (which relies on font underline thickness) in a project contradicts this. The underline does scale there. Since this isn't exposed to scripting, I think you could remove the `* theme_cache.base_scale` multiplier (with a comment to explain why). Here's 200% editor scale with `* theme_cache.base_scale` removed (displayed at 100% scale unless you click on it): 100% editor scale | 200% editor scale (with multiplier removed) -|- |

Usability-wise, this is beyond welcome.
The code is quite daunting, but I would expect nothing less due to how much is required to properly draw the squiggles (part of the reason why it wasn't present before this PR). I did still carefully look at the code.

I do appreciate the additional comments in `text_edit.cpp` for the line squiggles. One would usually say that the code has to explain itself, but this time it'd be difficult for it to. Still, some of them may be a bit excessive, or worth shuffling around to flow better.
